::: {#exr-miller-taylor-exp-base}
#### Linear Taylor polynomial of the exponential

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.20.

Find the first two terms (degree 1) of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = e^x$$

at $x_0 = 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-exp-base}
Since

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(0) &= e^0 \\
&= 1
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
f'(0) &= e^0 \\
&= 1:
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_1(x)
&= f(0) + f'(0)x \\
&= 1 + x
\end{aligned}
$$

The full Taylor series is

$$
\begin{aligned}
e^x &= \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} \\
&= 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{6} + \dots.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
